agree.reason: A wary backer who has lost money on a first-time creator gets what they look for: plain admissions, finished art and rules, a signed quote, a cost breakdown, regular updates and a refund pledge, so they would probably pledge.

honest.reason: The writer reframes 'proven hit' as 'proven at the table' and says outright that the game isn't a hit yet; the only small embellishments are 'every session showed me something to fix' and calling the sign-ups people 'already waiting'.

works_the_facts.reason: It works out the 572 backers needed, notes that this is fewer than half the 1,240 sign-ups, and adds up shipping and fees, but it leaves about $2,650 of the goal unexplained and understates plays per person (more than twice, when 140 multi-player sessions imply far more).

right_comparison.reason: The alternative, a finished game that never gets printed, is stated clearly, but the pitch doesn't explain what happens if the campaign falls short, and it treats sign-ups as near-backers without any conversion realism.

qualification.reason: The promises are checkable, with dates and consequences: delivery in November 2027, a refund if it is more than three months late, updates every two weeks, and an explicit statement that there are no stretch goals.

objections.reason: It meets the first-time-creator objection head on and admits up front that the ratings are few and mostly from convention tables, though a careful reader would still ask about the uncosted remainder of the goal and about shipping outside the US.

fit.reason: It is a pitch of roughly the requested 500 words, but it never names the game (Lantern Winter) or the creator, and it leaves out the campaign dates, which is a strange omission on a crowdfunding page.
